landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.

hotel.how.title: How to Make a Hotel Lobby AI Video
hotel.how.one.title: Pick two clear portraits
hotel.how.one.text: Choose one clear photo for each performer. A visible face, natural expression and similar camera angle give the video model a stronger reference for keeping two people distinct.
hotel.how.two.title: Set the timing
hotel.how.two.text: Write a simple sequence: person A begins, person B reacts, then the lead changes. A fixed camera and small gestures usually make the first attempt easier to judge.
hotel.how.three.title: Generate and review
hotel.how.three.text: Press generate, choose a plan, and we compose both people in the orange booth before transferring the Hotel Lobby performance and audio onto them. Review identity, hands, the center microphone and left-right placement before you share.
hotel.ideas.title: Hotel Lobby AI Ideas for Friends, Siblings and Couples
hotel.ideas.description: The duet works best when the relationship between the two performers is easy to understand. Start with one moment, one camera angle and a clear handoff.
hotel.ideas.friends.title: Friends on the mic
hotel.ideas.friends.text: Make a call and response: one friend takes the first line, the other answers at the mic. Use eye contact, smiles and small gestures to show their connection.
hotel.ideas.siblings.title: Sibling back and forth
hotel.ideas.siblings.text: One sibling starts confidently; the other joins on the next beat. Keep them on opposite sides of the orange booth and let their expressions tell the story.
hotel.ideas.couples.title: Couples in sync
hotel.ideas.couples.text: Give a couple a quiet first verse and a shared chorus. Keep the gestures small and let a glance across the microphone mark the moment they come together.
hotel.bottom.title: The mic is waiting.
hotel.bottom.text: Choose your two performers and make the lobby scene your own.
hotel.footer.line: Create a two-person AI duet video with Hotel Lobby AI.

hotel.explainer.title: What is the Hotel Lobby AI filter?
hotel.explainer.origin: The trend comes from a real performance. On June 17, 2022, the COLORS YouTube channel released Quavo and Takeoff performing their song "Hotel Lobby" against a flat orange backdrop, trading lines on a single microphone hung from the ceiling. In September 2026 creators on TikTok and X began using AI video tools to swap the two rappers for friends, couples, celebrities, fictional characters and even pets while keeping the original moves, lip-sync and audio — and the "Hotel Lobby AI" meme took off.
hotel.explainer.one: Two subjects stand on opposite sides of one hanging microphone while the camera holds steady. One leads, the other reacts, and then they trade the moment. Friends, partners or family members can appear together even when their source photos were taken separately.
hotel.explainer.two: This page makes that look for you. Choose two portraits, decide who appears on each side and optionally add a styling note. We compose the scene with GPT Image 2 and animate it with DreamActor motion transfer, which carries over the reference performance and its audio.
hotel.explainer.three: Think of it as a short scene. A good result keeps each person recognizable, gives both people room and places the microphone between them. Orange walls, warm light and a steady camera unify the setup. Results vary with the model and photos, so review the clip before posting.
hotel.guide.title: Make your Hotel Lobby AI duet look more like your people
hotel.guide.intro: A precise prompt helps, but the photos you choose set the ceiling for the final scene. These checks can reduce common identity and composition problems before you generate.
hotel.guide.photos.title: Start with useful portraits
hotel.guide.photos.text: Use sharp images with full faces and enough clothing to guide the scene. Avoid heavy filters, sunglasses, crowded backgrounds and cropped faces. Similar lighting and perspective can make the duet feel more consistent. If one portrait is a close-up and the other shows a full body, crop or replace one so the references match more closely. Neutral expressions leave more room for a believable reaction. Only transform images you have permission to use.
hotel.guide.motion.title: Keep the action readable
hotel.guide.motion.text: Describe one short exchange: a lead singer, a listening reaction and a handoff. Ask for natural mouth movement and small gestures while the camera stays centered. State whose lips move in each beat so the performers do not appear to sing the same line at once. Fast turns and sudden cuts can make faces or left-right positions harder to preserve.
hotel.guide.review.title: Inspect the first take
hotel.guide.review.text: Watch the clip before sharing. Confirm that A stays left, B stays right and the microphone stays between them. Check for warped hands, merged faces, extra people or changing outfits. Watch once with the sound off: the handoff should still make visual sense. If a face changes midway, shorten the scene before adding more movement. If the scene breaks, simplify your direction and try again.
hotel.prompt.title: Hotel Lobby AI Prompt (Copy and Paste)
hotel.prompt.one: For a Hotel Lobby AI duet, the starter prompt names the main visual anchors: a vertical 9:16 frame, a matte-orange booth, two separate people, one black microphone, soft light and a locked camera. It also asks the model to preserve faces and outfits and avoid side swaps, added people, captions and watermarks. These constraints give the generator a clearer shot list than a vague request to make two photos sing together.
hotel.prompt.two: Use the direction field for one styling detail, such as outfits, accessories or expressions. Keep it short so the core composition still leads — the booth, the center microphone and left-right placement are fixed by the base prompt. If the first result is off, change one thing at a time and generate again.
hotel.prompt.copy_text: Two people from my two reference photos perform a duet in a seamless burnt-orange recording booth. Person A (photo 1) stands on the left, Person B (photo 2) on the right, facing each other across one black microphone hanging at face level in the exact center. Vertical 9:16, static centered camera, soft even studio light, framed from the knees up. A sings the first line while B listens and nods; B takes the next line while A reacts; then they share the mic. Natural lip-sync and small hand gestures. Keep each face, hairstyle and outfit unchanged. No side swaps, no extra people, no captions, no watermark.
hotel.faq.title: Hotel Lobby AI FAQ
hotel.faq.one.question: Can I generate the duet video on this page?
hotel.faq.one.answer: Yes. Sign in, upload one photo for each side and press Generate. The scene is ready in under a minute and the finished video in about 3–5 minutes. Each video uses credits.
hotel.faq.two.question: What happens to my photos?
hotel.faq.two.answer: When you press Generate, your two photos are resized in your browser and sent to our AI provider (fal.ai) to create the scene and the video. They are not uploaded before you press Generate. Only use photos you have permission to use.
hotel.faq.three.question: Can I make the duet with two separate photos?
hotel.faq.three.answer: Yes. Use one clear reference for each person, with A on the left and B on the right. Identity preservation depends on the generator and photos, so inspect the result.
hotel.faq.four.question: Why do the faces or positions change in my result?
hotel.faq.four.answer: Models can drift when references are unclear or actions are busy. Use visible faces, remove camera moves and describe a shorter exchange. Repeat left-right placement and request one continuous shot. A usable clip may take several tries.
hotel.faq.five.question: Can I use photos of a couple or friends?
hotel.faq.five.answer: Yes. The orange booth can frame a couple, friends or family — including a parent and their child, as long as you're that child's parent or legal guardian. Change the performance direction but keep identities separate. Get permission from everyone pictured and identify the result as AI-generated when you share it.
hotel.faq.six.question: How much does a Hotel Lobby AI video cost?
hotel.faq.six.answer: Every generation uses credits, and the exact amount is shown on the button and in the pricing section. Choose a one-time pack or subscribe monthly. If a generation fails, the credits go back to your balance automatically.
hotel.faq.seven.question: What is the hotel lobby AI trend?
hotel.faq.seven.answer: It is a two-person duet scene in an orange recording booth. One person starts a line beside a hanging microphone, and the other responds. Creators often use two separate photos to plan a shared AI video scene.
hotel.faq.eight.question: Is the video generated on this site?
hotel.faq.eight.answer: Yes. The scene preview and the finished video are both generated here on Hotel Lobby AI — you don't need any other app or account. Finished videos are saved in My videos.

wc.faq.title: WordCraftApp questions, answered
wc.faq.free.q: Do I need to pay or create an account?
wc.faq.free.a: Our guides and hosted browser editor are free to use, and no WordCraftApp account is required to read, download or try online. WordCraft itself is open-source software under the MIT or Apache-2.0 license.
wc.faq.who.q: Who makes WordCraft? Is this the official site?
wc.faq.who.a: WordCraft is developed by the ArtCraft team. WordCraftApp is an independent English-language guide with download help, an online editor entry point, tutorials and comparisons. The developers' product page is getartcraft.com/apps/wordcraft.
wc.faq.docx.q: Can WordCraft open my Word documents?
wc.faq.docx.a: Yes. It opens and saves .docx natively and imports older Word 97-2003 .doc files. Because WordCraft is still in alpha, keep a copy of important documents and check complex layouts (charts, SmartArt) after a round trip.
wc.faq.ready.q: Can it fully replace Microsoft Word today?
wc.faq.ready.a: That depends on your documents and workflow. Our comparison covers WordCraft's advantages and limitations, including file compatibility and collaboration. Try copies of your important documents first, especially if you rely on complex formatting, macros or Microsoft 365 services.
wc.faq.safe.q: Where do the download links go?
wc.faq.safe.a: Our desktop download links lead to the developers' GitHub releases at storytold/wordcraft. Use the download guide to choose your platform, then check the release notes and published checksums before installing.
wc.faq.online.q: How does the online version work?
wc.faq.online.a: The online link opens the WordCraft web build hosted on this site. The editor runs in your browser and lets you open local documents and save your work to your device. WordCraftApp does not provide a document cloud-storage service; our online guide explains how to start and save your work.
wc.faq.ai.a: ArtCraft builds its Crafting Apps with the help of AI coding tools, which is how a small team could reimplement a Word-class editor so quickly. The code is a clean-room implementation written in Rust from public specifications, and it is all open for anyone to read.

wc.dl.meta_desc: Official WordCraft download links for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD, with step-by-step install guide, checksums and troubleshooting for ArtCraft WordCraft.
wc.dl.title: WordCraft download
wc.dl.subtitle: Free for every platform. Pick your system below. Every link goes straight to the official ArtCraft WordCraft release on GitHub.
wc.dl.not_sure: Not sure which file? Use WordCraft online instead, nothing to install.
wc.dl.verify_desc: Each release ships SHA256SUMS.txt. Compare it with the checksum of the file you downloaded:
wc.dl.win.s1: Download the x64 .msi installer (or ARM64 for Snapdragon laptops).
wc.dl.win.s2: Double-click the .msi and follow the setup wizard. The installer is code-signed by the publisher.
wc.dl.win.s3: Launch WordCraft from the Start menu. Prefer no install? Unzip the portable .zip and run wordcraft.exe.
wc.dl.mac.s1: Download the universal .dmg. It runs natively on Apple silicon and Intel.
wc.dl.mac.s2: Open the .dmg and drag WordCraft into your Applications folder.
wc.dl.mac.s3: Launch it from Applications. If macOS warns about the app, Control-click it and choose Open, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
wc.dl.linux.s1: AppImage (any distro): make it executable, then run it.
wc.dl.linux.s2: Debian / Ubuntu: install the .deb with apt.
wc.dl.linux.s3: Fedora / openSUSE: install the .rpm; or use the Flatpak bundle.
wc.dl.trouble.win_gpu.q: Windows: the app flashes and closes
wc.dl.trouble.win_gpu.a: WordCraft uses DirectX 12 by default. Some graphics drivers crash on start; try the Vulkan backend from PowerShell in the app folder:
wc.dl.trouble.old_pc.q: Windows: slow on an older PC
wc.dl.trouble.old_pc.a: If your graphics card has no DirectX 12 driver, Windows falls back to software rendering. Update your graphics driver, or use the online version in a modern browser.
wc.dl.trouble.logs.q: Where are the logs for a bug report?
wc.dl.trouble.logs.a: Windows: %APPDATA%\WordCraft\logs\ · macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/WordCraft/logs/ · Linux: ~/.config/wordcraft/logs/. Attach wordcraft.log when you report a bug on GitHub or Discord.

wc.tut.meta_title: WordCraft Tutorial: Beginner's Guide to the Free Word Alternative
wc.tut.meta_desc: Learn WordCraft step by step: the ribbon, styles, lists, tables, pictures, track changes, references, PDF export, keyboard shortcuts and the CLI.
wc.tut.title: WordCraft tutorial
wc.tut.subtitle: A practical beginner's guide to the WordCraft app. If you know Word, skim the headings: most things work exactly the way you expect.
wc.tut.start.p1: Install WordCraft from the download guide, or open the online version. On first launch you land on the File tab start page.
wc.tut.start.l1: Pick Blank document to start from scratch, or a template such as Letter, Résumé, Report or the Studio handbook sample.
wc.tut.start.l2: Choose Open to load an existing .docx, .doc, .odt, .rtf, .md or .txt file. Recent documents appear in the list below.
wc.tut.start.l3: The interface follows your system language. Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, German and 15+ more are built in.
wc.tut.ui.h: 2. Find your way around the ribbon
wc.tut.ui.p1: The ribbon has the same tabs as Word. Each tab groups related commands:
wc.tut.ui.file: File: new, open, save, export to PDF, document properties.
wc.tut.ui.home: Home: clipboard, font, paragraph, Styles gallery, find and replace.
wc.tut.ui.insert: Insert: tables, pictures, shapes, links, headers and footers, fields, symbols.
wc.tut.ui.design: Design and Layout: themes, margins, orientation, columns, breaks, watermark.
wc.tut.ui.refs: References and Mailings: TOC, footnotes, citations, mail merge, envelopes.
wc.tut.ui.review: Review and View: spelling, comments, track changes, zoom, Navigation pane, dark mode.
wc.tut.ui.p2: Can't find a button? Use command search. Every one of WordCraft's 422 commands can be found by name.
wc.tut.format.p1: Select text and use the Home tab, or the usual shortcuts, to change font, size, colour, bold, italic and underline. Format Painter copies formatting from one place to another.
wc.tut.format.p2: For headings, use Styles instead of manual formatting: click in a paragraph and choose Heading 1, Heading 2 or Title in the Styles gallery. Hovering previews the style live. Headings then appear in the Navigation pane and in your table of contents.
wc.tut.format.p3: Type * or 1. followed by a space to start a list. Enter continues the list, Tab demotes an item and Shift+Tab promotes it.
wc.tut.tables.p1: Insert → Table lets you drag out a grid. Table styles add banded rows; header rows repeat on every page. You can merge and split cells, sort rows and convert text to a table.
wc.tut.tables.p2: Insert → Pictures adds images you can crop, recolour and wrap text around (square, top and bottom, behind or in front of text).
wc.tut.tables.p3: On the Layout tab set margins, orientation, paper size and columns, and insert page or section breaks. Headers, footers and page numbers live on the Insert tab.
wc.tut.review.p1: On the Review tab, turn on Track Changes. Insertions and deletions are marked in colour, and each one can be accepted or rejected, one by one or all at once.
wc.tut.review.p2: Select text and click New Comment to add a comment balloon in the margin. Compare Documents shows the differences between two versions of a file.
wc.tut.review.p3: Spelling and grammar are checked as you type, offline. Press F7 to step through suggestions.
wc.tut.refs.h: 6. Table of contents, footnotes and citations
wc.tut.refs.p1: Once your headings use Heading styles, References → Table of Contents builds a TOC with page numbers. Update it after editing.
wc.tut.refs.p2: Insert footnotes and endnotes, add sources and citations in APA, MLA, Chicago or IEEE style, then insert a bibliography, captions, a table of figures or an index.
wc.tut.save.p1: Save keeps your document as .docx, so colleagues using Word can open it. Use Save As to choose .odt, .rtf, .html, .md, .tex or .txt.
wc.tut.save.p2: File → Export → PDF creates a PDF with real, selectable text, working links and bookmarks.
wc.tut.save.p3: Tip: WordCraft is in alpha. Keep a backup of important files and check complex documents after saving.
wc.tut.keys.p1: WordCraft follows Word's shortcuts. On a Mac use ⌘ instead of Ctrl.
wc.tut.keys.bold: Bold the selection, or the word under the caret

wc.vs.meta_title: WordCraft vs Microsoft Word: Differences, Pros and Cons (2026)
wc.vs.meta_desc: WordCraft vs Microsoft Word compared honestly: price, license, platforms, .docx compatibility, offline use, AI features, collaboration and maturity of ArtCraft WordCraft.
wc.vs.title: WordCraft vs Microsoft Word
wc.vs.subtitle: Both open and save .docx and share the same ribbon layout. The differences are price, openness and platforms, and how mature each one is.
wc.vs.win1.d: Word is part of a paid Microsoft 365 plan or a one-time Office purchase. WordCraft costs nothing, on every device, forever.
wc.vs.win2.d: MIT or Apache-2.0. Anyone can read the code, fix bugs, self-host the web build or ship it inside their own product.
wc.vs.win3.t: A real Linux and BSD app
wc.vs.win3.d: Word has no Linux version. WordCraft runs natively on Linux (x86_64, ARM64, RISC-V) and FreeBSD.
wc.vs.win4.d: No account, no cloud sign-in. Spelling and grammar run on your machine.
wc.vs.win5.d: Native Rust on the GPU, with no Electron. Re-layout of a 188-page document takes about 1.4 ms per keystroke.
wc.vs.win6.d: A CLI, a JSON control channel and an MCP server expose all 422 commands to scripts and AI agents. No VBA required.
wc.vs.word1: Maturity: decades of polish, and pagination that is the reference every other app is measured against.
wc.vs.word2: Real-time co-authoring and sharing through OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams.
wc.vs.word3: Microsoft Copilot for drafting and rewriting inside the document.
wc.vs.word4: Charts, SmartArt and complex documents survive every round trip.
wc.vs.word5: Mobile apps for iOS and Android, and enterprise support and administration.
wc.vs.who_wc1: write essays, reports, letters, CVs or books and don't want to pay for a subscription
wc.vs.who_wc2: use Linux, or a mix of operating systems
wc.vs.who_wc3: care about privacy and open source
wc.vs.who_wc4: want to automate documents with scripts or AI agents
wc.vs.who_word1: co-author documents live with a team in Microsoft 365
wc.vs.who_word2: depend on VBA macros, complex templates or SmartArt
wc.vs.who_word3: need guaranteed pixel-perfect fidelity for legal or print work
wc.vs.migrate1: Try WordCraft online first with a copy of a real document you work on.
wc.vs.migrate2: Keep using .docx. It is WordCraft's native format, so you can move back and forth.
wc.vs.migrate3: Rely on Styles rather than manual formatting; styled documents convert most cleanly.
wc.vs.sources: Facts are from the WordCraft README and roadmap (October 2026) and Microsoft's Word product page. WordCraft changes fast, so check the official pages for the latest.

wc.faq.artcraft.a: ArtCraft WordCraft is the full name people search for. ArtCraft is the team and community behind a family of free Crafting Apps, and WordCraft is their word processor. Its siblings include PhotoCraft for images, VectorCraft for illustration and GridCraft for spreadsheets.
wc.faq.req.q: What are the WordCraft system requirements?
wc.faq.req.a: The desktop app runs on Windows 10 and 11, current macOS on Apple silicon or Intel, most 64-bit Linux distributions and FreeBSD 14. It draws with the GPU through DirectX 12, Metal or Vulkan and falls back to software rendering on older PCs. WordCraft online needs a recent browser with WebGPU or WebGL2.
